title: Circular Measure Module 4 Lesson 2: Two-Centre Overlaps & Shared Chords custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values, configurations and requested combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs reasoning scope only.

parts.prompt: In a triangle $\triangle PQR$, $PQ = 6\text{ cm}$, $PR = 8\text{ cm}$ and $QR = 10\text{ cm}$. A circular arc centred at $P$ with radius $6\text{ cm}$ subtends the angle $\angle QPR$. Find the exact length of this arc in terms of $\pi$.

Two circular arcs are drawn with the same centre $O$ and subtend the same angle $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. The radii of the two arcs are $4\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$. Find the exact sum of the lengths of the two arcs.

In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 6\text{ cm}$, $AC = 5\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 7\text{ cm}$. A circular arc centred at $A$ of radius $6\text{ cm}$ subtends angle $\angle BAC$. Use the cosine rule to find the exact value of $\cos(\angle BAC)$.
A circle has radius $8\text{ cm}$. A minor arc subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact length of the corresponding major arc in terms of $\pi$.

A chord $PQ$ of length $12\text{ cm}$ lies in a circle of radius $10\text{ cm}$ centred at $O$. Find the exact value of $\sin\theta$, where $\theta = \angle POQ / 2$ is the half-angle subtended by the chord at the centre.

Two circles have radii $5\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$. State the exact range of possible values for the distance $d$ between their centres such that the two circles intersect at exactly two distinct points.
A triangle $APB$ has $AP=6$ cm, $BP=8$ cm and $AB=10$ cm. Two separate arcs are centred at $P$, have radii $6$ cm and $8$ cm, and each subtends $\angle APB$. Find their combined length.
